description: Free and Open Source Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)

sources.entry: ERPNext - ERP system to help you run your business. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Python/Docker
ERPNext | Free and open-source ERP for businesses

summary.one_liner: ERPNext is a free, open-source ERP system for running a business, covering accounting, inventory and orders, manufacturing, asset management, and projects.
summary.what_it_does: ERPNext is a web-based enterprise resource planning application built on the Frappe Framework. According to the README, it covers accounting (recording transactions through financial reporting), order management (inventory levels, replenishment, sales orders, customers, suppliers, shipments, and fulfillment), and manufacturing (production cycle, material consumption tracking, capacity planning, and subcontracting). It also handles asset management from purchase to disposal and project delivery with tasks, timesheets, and issues tracked by project. The README names Frappe Framework (Python and JavaScript, with a database abstraction layer, authentication, and REST API) and Frappe UI (a Vue-based component library) as its foundations. Topics also list CRM, HR, healthcare, point-of-sale, retail, and support, though the README body itself only details the features above.
use_cases: run day-to-day business operations in one system
track inventory and fulfill sales orders
manage invoices and accounting with financial reports
plan production and track material consumption
track company assets from purchase to disposal
manage internal and external projects with timesheets
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL>  (the README's clone URL is blank in the source; use the frappe_docker repo)
Wait for the create-site container to finish, then open port 8080 (user: Administrator, password: admin)
Manual dev install: use the bench install script, then run 'bench start' and 'bench new-site erpnext.localhost'
bench get-app <ERPNext URL> && bench --site erpnext.localhost install-app erpnext
notable: Fully open-source ERP covering accounting, inventory, manufacturing, assets, and projects in one system
Built on the Frappe Framework, which provides a REST API and user authentication
Official Docker demo setup with a single compose command
Install script for bench sets up dependencies such as MariaDB and generates passwords
Managed hosting option through Frappe Cloud
caveats: The Docker setup is explicitly a disposable demo; custom apps cannot be installed to it and production needs the full documentation
Production deployment requires separate configuration documented elsewhere
Default demo credentials are published in the README and should be changed
